stem: After assessing harm risk in a child or adolescent, which set of broad next-step pathways is correct?

options.text: Child Protection Helpline, Child Wellbeing Unit, or continue to monitor and support
Emergency department admission, police referral, or discharge to the general practitioner only
Child Protection Unit review, court application, or school suspension
Child Wellbeing Unit, forensic examination, or automatic foster placement
Mandatory admission, e-report, or no documentation

explanation: The correct pathways are Child Protection Helpline, Child Wellbeing Unit, or continue to monitor and support. These are the three broad next steps after assessing harm risk in a child or adolescent.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Correct because these are the three broad next-step pathways described after assessing harm risk.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because emergency admission, police referral, and GP-only discharge are not the standard three pathways in this framework.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because Child Protection Unit review, court application, and school suspension are not the listed broad outcomes after risk assessment.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because forensic examination and automatic foster placement are not part of the broad pathway summary, even though Child Wellbeing Unit is included.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because mandatory admission, e-report, and no documentation are not the documented pathway options after risk assessment.
